Discussion thread

The original post asks whether remote work improves productivity for software teams when async communication norms are documented clearly from the start.

I have worked remotely for six years and find written decision logs more valuable than daily video standups that could have been a short document instead.

Agreed on decision logs. We also keep a single source of truth wiki so newcomers are not lost in chat history from months ago.

Hybrid schedules work when teams overlap four hours for pairing and leave deep work blocks protected on calendar for the rest of the day without meeting creep.
